verdicts.reason: A crams the NEW VIDEO pill and the VOLTSTRIDE logo into one top row with almost no gap, so they compete; the green circle sits on its own in the bottom-right corner, no longer behind the shoe; and the subhead is nearly headline-sized. B gives the logo a clean centred spot above a clear headline-subhead-shoe sequence, but it has the same detached circle, and its tilted pill awkwardly overlaps the edge of the circle.

A has a cramped top row with the pill and logo nearly touching, a subhead too close in size to the headline, and the green circle cut off from the shoe. B shrinks the headline, leaves a dead band between the shoe and the copy, and pushes a tiny pill into the bottom-left of the cropped circle, which weakens both the hierarchy and the pill.

A reduces the shoe and the VOLTSTRIDE logo to tiny, unreadable bits at the bottom, squeezed against the circle, and leaves the top third empty, so the brand is effectively gone. B has a cramped pill and logo row and a circle cut off from the shoe, but the brand, headline and product stay legible.

A has the same cramped pill and logo row at the top, subhead nearly as big as the headline, and green circle split off from the shoe. B crops the shoe against the top edge of the canvas, leaves a tiny pill floating under the subhead, and drops the logo to the bottom-left, where its last letters run into the circle.
